result: Do not open arbitrary configured stdio MCP discovery with the current finite subprocess cleanup guarantee. Preserve the gap while continuing independently implementable management work.
officialSourceFindings: mcpServerStatus/list without threadId reports a new discovery snapshot; runtimeStatus null is not current conversation status.
The implementation creates a new eager MCP connection set even with a loaded threadId; repeated calls may launch distinct processes.
Some MCP stdio children create independent process groups. Parent process reap, parent group disappearance and pipe EOF do not prove those groups stopped.
EOF supports graceful app-server exit but the ephemeral collector does not await an all-descendant exit barrier. No reviewed public shutdown RPC returns that barrier.
ACP mcp/message is a different unstable transport, not enumeration of this Agent configured tools. The reviewed adapter does not provide this alternate enumeration/cleanup surface.

counterexamples: Primary group gone plus EOF while exact self-owned independent child remained alive.
Parent exit before delayed KILL worker completed prevented that worker from running.
syntheticValidation.positiveControl: An owner retained through exact child reap can observe complete cleanup; current official response does not expose that mechanism.
syntheticValidation.boundary: Synthetic Python peers only; no real official CLI, MCP server, user configuration or production code mutation. Original observation EPERM retained; refused checks are unknown, not success.
